newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ex-pm Shamir predicts early end to Hebron accord.
newsitem.headline: Ex-pm Shamir predicts early end to Hebron accord.

text.p: Former Israeli prime minister Yitzhak Shamir savaged a deal extending Palestinian control to the West Bank town of Hebron on Wednesday, calling it a defeat for Israel that would trigger violence.
"This accord is very bad for Israel, it's a defeat we have inflicted upon ourselves," Shamir, hardline prime minister from 1986 to 1992, told France's Europe 1 radio.

On the border between Israel and the Gaza on Tuesday night, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat sealed the U.S.-brokered accord on Hebron and agreed a timetable for further Israeli pullbacks.
"This isn't peace. Each capitulation does not bring peace, it brings the contrary. It's violence," Shamir said.
Aged 81 and former head of Netanyahu's right-wing Likud Party, Shamir predicted the accord would collapse even though he thought that the Israeli parliament would ratify the pact.
"I don't think that (the accord) will last a long time," he said. He said that one consolation from a self-inflicted defeat was that "we can ourselves correct the situation and change it."
Shamir, a former Jewish guerrilla and spy, has consistently opposed to returning what he considers to be Israeli land to Palestinians under the terms of the Oslo peace accords.
